screening_decisions.reason: This is an observational retrospective study analyzing complications from 5,851 consecutive first-trimester abortions. It is NOT a randomized controlled trial and does NOT compare different surgical methods. The study only describes complication rates and risk factors.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (conventional vacuum aspiration vs manual vacuum aspiration) for first-trimester abortion (less than 56 days gestation). 200 women were randomized to VA or MVA. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical methods, first-trimester population.

This is an epidemiological/observational study comparing mortality and morbidity trends before and after the Roe v Wade decision. It uses national statistics data from CDC and other sources. It is NOT a randomized controlled trial and does NOT compare different surgical methods.

Although this is a randomized controlled trial, it compares prostaglandin suppository vs placebo for cervical preparation before vacuum aspiration. This is a medical intervention (cervical preparation) rather than a comparison of different surgical methods. All patients received vacuum aspiration - the same surgical method. Does not meet selection criteria for comparing different surgical methods.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (D&C vs vacuum aspiration) for first-trimester abortion. 420 women were randomly assigned to D&C or VA groups. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical methods, first-trimester population (6-12 weeks gestation).

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (manual vacuum aspiration vs electric vacuum aspiration) for first-trimester abortion (less than 10 weeks gestation). 84 women were randomized to manual or electric vacuum aspiration. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical methods, first-trimester population.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (manual vacuum aspiration vs electric vacuum aspiration) for first-trimester abortion. 127 women (64 MVA, 63 EVA) were randomly assigned. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical methods, first-trimester population.

This study compares vacuum aspiration (23 women) vs classical dilatation and curettage (24 women) in first-trimester abortion. However, the abstract does NOT state that women were randomized. It appears to be a non-randomized comparative study. Does not meet the selection criteria requiring randomized controlled trials.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (metal cannulae vs flexible plastic cannulae) for vacuum aspiration in first-trimester abortion (7-10 weeks gestation). 300 subjects were randomly assigned. While both use vacuum aspiration, they represent different surgical instruments/methods. Meets selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical approaches, first-trimester population.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two surgical methods (manual vacuum aspirator vs electric vacuum curettage) for first-trimester abortion. 114 women were randomized. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, compares different surgical methods, first-trimester population.
